exercise.name: 1 2 Stick Drill

reference.title: 1 2 Stick Drill (male)
reference.listing: Animated GIF; data sheet: body part Plyometrics, equipment Stick, exercise type Aerobic
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original. Some sources use the same name for a step-and-hold (stick the landing) drill; this module follows the GymVisual pattern: continuous lateral quick feet over floor sticks.

equipment: 5-6 low sticks or flat markers (or an agility ladder laid flat)
exercise.laterality: Bilateral, alternating feet: lead with the right foot going right, the left foot coming back

muscleNotes.calves_r: Quick, springy push-offs and landings on the ball of the foot (gastrocnemius and soleus).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Quick, springy push-offs and landings on the ball of the foot (gastrocnemius and soleus).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Hold the quarter-squat stance and absorb each landing.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Hold the quarter-squat stance and absorb each landing.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Pushes the body sideways and keeps the pelvis level on each single-leg contact; works hardest pushing off when travelling left and catching the lead step when travelling right.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Pushes the body sideways and keeps the pelvis level on each single-leg contact.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Pull the trail foot in toward the lead foot.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Pull the trail foot in toward the lead foot.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Lift the foot just enough to clear each stick (our inference from the movement; not named in the sources).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Lift the foot just enough to clear each stick (our inference from the movement; not named in the sources).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Support the hip hinge with the gluteus maximus.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Support the hip hinge with the gluteus maximus.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk square and still while the feet move.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the chest up in the slight forward lean.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the chest up in the slight forward lean.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Lightly holds the hands at the chest.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Lightly holds the hands at the chest.

breathing.pattern: Breathe rhythmically and do not hold the breath. Each pass lasts only a few seconds, so steady, relaxed breathing is enough; some coaches cue breathing out as you step.
breathing.cadence: Natural breathing; about 3-4 foot contacts per second in the animation

prescription.work: 2-5 s per pass down the row
prescription.rest: Full recovery between passes; about 30-60 s as an app default (design estimate)
prescription.staticOption: Walking or marching tempo through the row
prescription.frequency: 2-3 sessions per week, often as about 10 minutes of the warm-up (ladder trials ran 6-10 weeks)
prescription.tempo: Start at a walking or marching pace; speed up only while contacts stay light and accurate

cues.text: Stand at one end of the row, side-on to it: feet hip-width, quarter squat, chest up, hands clasped at the chest.
Lead foot over the stick into the next gap, trail foot right behind it: 1-2, 1-2, on the balls of the feet. Never cross the feet.
Stop under control at the end: stay low, hips square to the front.
Come back leading with the other foot. Hips stay at the same height and the head stays level.
Stop, reset the stance, then go again. Light and quiet contacts; pick the feet up just enough to clear the sticks.

mistakes.mistake: Crossing the feet or reaching with long steps
mistakes.fix: Short, quick steps; the trail foot meets the lead foot, never passes it.

mistakes.mistake: Standing up tall or bobbing the head
mistakes.fix: Hold the quarter squat; the head moves sideways only, not up and down.
Land softly on the balls of the feet; aim for quiet contacts.
Knee tracks over the toes; slow down until it does.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning the shoulders toward the direction of travel
mistakes.fix: Keep hips, shoulders and torso parallel to the row; move the feet, not the trunk.
Glance at the row first, then eyes forward and use peripheral vision.

mistakes.mistake: Going faster than control allows (kicking sticks, missed contacts)
mistakes.fix: Master the pattern slowly first, then add speed.

kinematics.peak: 31–48° on the ground; up to ≈69° on the swing leg
kinematics.norm: Quarter squat, roughly 30-45° held nearly constant (design estimate; no published norm)
Similar hip hinge to the knee bend (design estimate)
Slightly forward, chest up; shoulders not leaning toward the direction of travel
Two quick contacts per gap, feet never cross
About 30-40 cm (estimate from the reference); ladder squares about 40-45 cm
Row length plus one stance width
Ground contacts as short as possible while staying controlled; not measured in any study found

kinematics.measure: Swing foot clearance over a stick
kinematics.norm: Just enough to clear the sticks

cautions: Low-load drill, but it loads the ankles and knees quickly in a sideways direction.
Use flat, non-slip ground and flat markers or sticks that will not roll underfoot.
Stop a set when contacts get heavy or the pattern breaks down; quality matters more than volume.
No study found reports injuries from quick-feet drills; injury risk has simply not been studied.
modify: Recent ankle sprain or chronic ankle instability, knee pain or recent knee ligament injury, Achilles or calf pain, balance problems or late pregnancy: check with a clinician and start slowly.
regressions: Walking or marching tempo through the row.
Wider spacing, or flat markers or tape lines instead of sticks.
One gap at a time with a pause after each 1-2.
progressions: Faster contacts while staying quiet and accurate.
Add a visual or auditory start or change-of-direction signal to make it reactive.
Longer row or several passes back and forth without stopping.
